docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:458:| 1 | **4.9.A** (W5-133, shipped) | `ReferenceMode` + `Locale {EnUs, De, Fr}` in `ql-types::eval_context`; `LocaleData` + `locale_data()` in `ql-formula-syntax::locale`; `Workbook::reference_mode` / `locale` accessors in `ql-storage`. Layering refined during implementation — enums in `ql-types`, separator data in `ql-formula-syntax`, no new dep-graph edge. |
docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:463:| 3 | **4.9.C parser** (W5-139, shipped) + **4.9.C binder** (W5-140, shipped) | **Parser (W5-139):** `Token::R1C1Ref` → intermediate `Expr::R1C1Ref { sheet, row_axis, col_axis }` (new variant) + `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` for ranges. Per-axis mixed-relativity check rejects with `ParseError::R1C1MixedRelativity`. Refined the design wording "Expr::CellRef with intermediate markers" to a new variant — keeps the 50+ `CellAddr` construction sites untouched. **Binder (W5-140):** `bind_with_context_v2` lowers `Expr::R1C1Ref` → `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet, row, col, abs_col, abs_row }` using `BindSite::at_cell` for relative axes. Absolute axes drop straight in as `n - 1` (0-indexed). Relative axes resolve against `site.cell` (None → `BindError::R1C1RequiresAnchor`). Out-of-grid resolution → `BindError::R1C1OutOfBounds { resolved_row, resolved_col }`. The `abs_col` / `abs_row` flags on the emitted `ExprPlan::CellRef` are derived per-axis from the `AxisSpec` variant — preserves the abs/rel distinction the printer needs at 4.9.D. **Range lowering deferred** — `RangeRef::R1C1Cells` still surfaces via the existing `Expr::RangeRef(_)` `UnsupportedVariant` path (same as absolute `RangeRef::Cells`); range binding is handled by the existing aggregate-function dispatch and will fold R1C1Cells when that wave touches it. Calcgraph + printer `unreachable!()` stubs unchanged: storage canon (§ 4.4) lowers R1C1 → A1 text before fingerprint / stripe registration. |
docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:467:| 7 | **4.9.G** (W5-143, shipped, parser+printer-only) | `Token::At` (standalone `@`) + `Expr::ImplicitIntersection(Box<Expr>)` AST variant. Parser treats `@` as a prefix unary at bp 70 — looser than range `:` (so `@A:A` parses as `@(A:A)`, the Excel canon), tighter than every binary operator. Sheet-prefix interaction: `apply_sheet_to_term` gets a new arm that recurses INTO `ImplicitIntersection` to stamp the sheet onto the inner ref (so `Sheet1!@A1` and `@Sheet1!A1` produce identical ASTs). Walker touchpoints closed per Sonnet H-1: arms added to `rewrite_sheet_name_in_expr`, `rewrite_table_ref`, `rewrite_column_ref`, `print_expr_ctx`, `plan::variant_kind`, and `ql-calcgraph::fingerprint::hash_expr` (tag byte 13). **Binder stub** returns `BindError::UnsupportedVariant` pointing to 4.9.H (mirrors the 4.9.C pre-binder pattern). The in-bracket `@` inside `Sales[@Col]` stays inside `Token::StructuredRef.bracket_content` per OOXML escape rules — never reaches the new `Token::At` arm. Two prior tests assuming `@foo` was a lex error were updated to use backtick instead. |
docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:472:| 12 | **4.9.L** (W5-148, shipped) | Round-trip + edge case verification suite. +12 end-to-end property tests in `workbook_runtime::tests`: mixed-relativity range rejection at set_formula, `Sales[@Col]` vs `@Sales[Qty]` semantic equivalence, `@A:A` / `@1:1` whole-range narrowing at anchor, `Sheet1!@A1` cross-sheet, R1C1+EN round-trip through op-log replay (set_reference_mode + set_formula both replayed), DE+EN round-trip through replay, `@` preservation through replay, reference_mode/locale changes leave stored text canonical, `@scalar` idempotency, `@SUM(scalar args)` no-op. Note: rule 7 (function-returns-array → top-left) deferred — array-returning functions in scalar context still return `#CALC!` per existing 4.7.G limit; closing megaudit (4.9.O) decides whether to bundle that with cell-boundary spill rewiring or defer to a Phase 4.10 polish item. |
docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:473:| 13 | **4.9.M** (W5-149, shipped) | Table-driven coverage matrix `(mode × locale × @-presence)` = 30 cells. Each cell specifies a `(mode, locale, input)` triple and the expected canonical (A1+EnUs) output; the driver runs `set_formula(0, 0, 0, input)` and asserts the stored text matches. Modes: A1, R1C1. Locales: EnUs, De, Fr. `@`-presence: none, prefix-cell, prefix-function, inside-arg, prefix-rel-ref. 3 test fns: full-matrix driver, no-duplicate-cells invariant, per-axis dimension counts (pins 2/3/30 so future cell-adds trip the axis sanity test until the doc is updated). Confirms the design § 4.4 canon: stored text is mode + locale invariant; `@` is preserved verbatim. |
docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:490:| Q8 `Sheet1!@A1` | First-class in 4.9.G/H grammar production (NOT edge-case test). Codex + Sonnet agree. |

   543	/// **W5-142 (Phase 4.9.F):** locale-aware number printer.
   544	///
   545	/// Replaces the canonical `.` decimal separator with the locale's
   546	/// decimal glyph in the formatted output. Rust's `f64` Display
   547	/// always emits `.` regardless of locale (it's a numeric, not
   548	/// locale-aware, formatter), so we do a single byte substitution.
   549	///
   550	/// Scientific notation (`1e10`) — `e`/`E` are locale-invariant per
   551	/// W5-135 design (numeric exponent marker is not separable from
   552	/// decimal-separator choice in the lex direction either).
   553	fn print_number_with_locale(n: f64, decimal_sep: char, out: &mut String) {
   554	    if n.fract() == 0.0 && n.abs() < 1.0e16 {
   555	        // Integer-valued f64 → no decimal point. Decimal sep irrelevant.
   556	        out.push_str(&format!("{}", n as i64));
   557	    } else {
   558	        let canonical = format!("{n}");
   559	        if decimal_sep == '.' {
   560	            // Hot path: EN locale emits the canonical form verbatim.
   561	            out.push_str(&canonical);
   562	        } else {
   563	            // DE/FR: swap `.` → locale glyph. f64 Display only emits a
   564	            // single `.` per number (no thousands sep in `{n}` output),
   565	            // so byte-level substitution is safe.
   566	            for c in canonical.chars() {
   567	                if c == '.' {
   568	                    out.push(decimal_sep);
   569	                } else {
   570	                    out.push(c);
   571	                }
   572	            }
   573	        }
   574	    }
   575	}

   663	            out.push_str(ev.sigil());
   664	            Ok(())
   665	        }
   666	        Expr::Array(rows) => {
   667	            // **W5-142 (Phase 4.9.F):** locale-aware array row/col
   668	            // separators. EN: row=`;`, col=`,`. DE/FR: row=`.`, col=`\\`.
   669	            // Both followed by space for readability.
   670	            if rows.is_empty() {
   671	                unreachable!(
   672	                    "print_expr_ctx: Expr::Array with zero rows — parser rejects empty \
   673	                     literals via ParseError::EmptyArrayLiteral; constructing one \
   674	                     directly is a programmer bug"
   675	                );
   676	            }
   677	            let ld = crate::locale::locale_data(ctx.locale);
   678	            let row_sep = ld.array_row_separator;
   679	            let col_sep = ld.array_col_separator;
   680	            out.push('{');
   681	            for (i, row) in rows.iter().enumerate() {
   682	                if i > 0 {
   683	                    out.push(row_sep);
   684	                    out.push(' ');
   685	                }
   686	                for (j, cell) in row.iter().enumerate() {
   687	                    if j > 0 {
   688	                        out.push(col_sep);
   689	                        out.push(' ');
   690	                    }
   691	                    print_expr_ctx(cell, ctx, out, 0)?;
   692	                }
   693	            }
   694	            out.push('}');
   695	            Ok(())
   696	        }
   697	        Expr::Spill(_) => {
   698	            unreachable!(
   699	                "print_expr_ctx: Expr::Spill is reserved for Phase 4.9 (Excel `A1#` syntax) \
   700	                 and not constructed in Phase 4.7 — reaching here means the AST was malformed"
   701	            );
   702	        }
   703	        Expr::StructuredRef { table_name, spec } => {
   704	            out.push_str(table_name);
   705	            out.push('[');
   706	            print_sref_spec(spec, out);
   707	            out.push(']');
   708	            Ok(())
   709	        }
   710	        // **W5-143 (Phase 4.9.G):** implicit-intersection — emit
   711	        // `@<inner>` for round-trip preservation. Inner is printed
   712	        // with prefix-unary-bp so future binary-context nesting
   713	        // re-parenthesizes correctly. Today's parser folds `@expr`
   714	        // greedily so `print(parse("@A1")) == "@A1"`.
   715	        Expr::ImplicitIntersection(inner) => {
   716	            out.push('@');
   717	            print_expr_ctx(inner, ctx, out, 70)
   718	        }
   719	        // **W5-141 (Phase 4.9.D):** intermediate R1C1 single ref. The
   720	        // emission path depends on `ctx.mode`:
   721	        //
   722	        // - `R1C1`: emit directly from `AxisSpec` verbatim — `R1C1`,
   723	        //   `R[-1]C[2]`, `RC` etc. Sheet prefix uses the existing
   724	        //   `print_sheet_prefix` (mode-agnostic glyph).
   725	        // - `A1`: resolve each `AxisSpec` to an absolute 0-indexed
   726	        //   coord (relative axes need `ctx.site`), then emit as a
   727	        //   regular A1 `CellAddr`. `AxisSpec::Abs(n)` → `$<letter><row>`
   728	        //   (absolute parts get `$` prefix); `AxisSpec::Rel(offset)`
   729	        //   resolves to an absolute coord but emits WITHOUT `$`
   730	        //   (Excel canon: relative R1C1 axes round-trip to non-abs A1).
   731	        Expr::R1C1Ref {
   732	            sheet,
   733	            row_axis,
   734	            col_axis,
   735	        } => {
   736	            print_sheet_prefix(sheet, out);
   737	            match ctx.mode {
   738	                ReferenceMode::R1C1 => {
   739	                    emit_r1c1_axis_from_spec(*row_axis, 'R', out);
   740	                    emit_r1c1_axis_from_spec(*col_axis, 'C', out);
   741	                    Ok(())
   742	                }
   743	                ReferenceMode::A1 => {
   744	                    let row = axis_spec_to_absolute_coord(*row_axis, ctx.site.map(|s| s.cell.row))?;
   745	                    let col = axis_spec_to_absolute_coord(*col_axis, ctx.site.map(|s| s.cell.col))?;
   746	                    if matches!(col_axis, AxisSpec::Abs(_)) {
   747	                        out.push('$');
   748	                    }
   749	                    out.push_str(&column_index_to_letters(col));
   750	                    if matches!(row_axis, AxisSpec::Abs(_)) {
   751	                        out.push('$');
   752	                    }
   753	                    out.push_str(&(row + 1).to_string());
   754	                    Ok(())
   755	                }
   756	            }
   757	        }
   758	    }
   759	}

The cache path does have a real integration hazard: `set_formula` canonicalizes the text, then keys the bound-plan cache only by `(canonical_text, sheet, name_gen)`, while `@` range narrowing is done during bind using the formula cell. I’m checking whether anything later rebinds with the correct address before evaluation or graph registration; if not, this is a ship blocker.

     1	//! Replay an `OpLog` against a `Workbook`.
     2	//!
     3	//! Phase 2A.3.a (2026-05-12): single entry point `replay_into(&OpLog, &mut
     4	//! Workbook, &FunctionRegistry) -> Result<usize, ReplayError>`. Returns the
     5	//! count of ops successfully applied; on failure, returns
     6	//! `ReplayError::At { index, kind }` carrying the position of the failing
     7	//! op and the underlying failure. The workbook is left in a partial state
     8	//! on failure (callers decide whether to discard, recover, or recompute).
     9	//!
    10	//! ## Replay semantics
    11	//!
    12	//! Each `Op` variant maps to one `Workbook` mutation:
    13	//!
    14	//! - `PutValue` → `Workbook::put_at` (after row/col bounds check).
    15	//! - `PutFormula` → `Workbook::put_formula` (text only; replay does NOT
    16	//!   re-evaluate — that's a separate step the caller drives via

    32	//! `add_sheet` all are). Callers wanting at-most-once semantics across
    33	//! sessions track replay state themselves (Phase 5+ work).

**HIGH** [workbook_runtime.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime.rs:592) lines 592-607, [plan.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-exec/src/plan.rs:973) lines 973-997: `PlanCacheKey` is not cell-specific, but `@` range narrowing is bind-time and anchor-dependent, so two cells with the same canonical text like `@A:A` or `@A1:A10` can reuse the first cell’s narrowed `CellRef`. Fix: include the formula address in the cache key for anchor-dependent formulas, or preserve `@` to eval time so the existing formula-cell env drives narrowing; add a two-cell regression that proves the second write does not cache-hit to the first row/col plan.
